steps: Picture each panel lying flat outside the frame after turning down.
Each side of the square grows outward by the width of the flattened panel.
Extending the outer edges until they meet gives a square of side 70 cm.
qs.trap: Forgetting that the panels lie outside the frame after turning, so the square grows on every side.

steps: Worst case: you keep pulling gloves that cannot pair.
There are 20 left gloves (10 blue, 10 white). You could pull all 20 lefts first.
The 21st glove must be a right glove, and it matches one of the lefts in colour.
So 21 gloves guarantee a pair.
qs.trap: Answering 3, as with socks. Gloves need a left and a right, not just the same colour.

steps: Each sheet has a month on each side: January front, February back, and so on.
A hole through a sheet appears mirrored on the back: Thursday on the front becomes Tuesday on the back, in the same row.
April is on a back side, like December: Tuesday, third row.
April 2024 starts on Monday, so the third-row Tuesday is the 16th.

steps: Count by type: small triangles at the star's points, triangles between points and pentagon sides, and larger ones.
Use the five-fold symmetry: count one type, multiply by 5.
Types: 5 star points, 5 small side triangles, 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 larger, and the 5 big ones from three pentagon corners.
The total is 35.
qs.trap: Missing large triangles made from three corners of the pentagon.

steps: The green triangle has side 2r (two radii) and height 1.73r.
The red triangle has its base along a row of centres, 4r long: twice as long.
Its third corner is one row away, so its height is also 1.73r.
Same height, double base: red = 2 × 3.14 = 6.28.

steps: To reach a house, the virus arrives from one house back or two houses back.
So ways(n) = ways(n − 1) + ways(n − 2): the Fibonacci pattern.
House 13: 233.

steps: Water pushed up by each object = its volume under water.
P: 64 × 9/10 = 57.6. Q: 50. R and S sink fully: 295.4 and 397. Total 800 cc.
Tank base = 40 × 20 = 800 cm², so the level falls by 800 ÷ 800 = 1 cm.
New depth = 10 − 1 = 9 cm.

steps: Lines may go beyond the grid, which is the key to saving lines.
Plan long lines that cross a full row, column or diagonal of 4 dots.
The start and end points fix where the first and last lines run.
Six lines are enough and five are not.
qs.trap: Staying inside the grid. Lines may extend past the outer dots.

steps: Compare letter shapes, not size or weight.
Look at the head-line, the curve of the "tha", and the stroke ends.
Group the words with matching shapes.
There are 7 groups.
qs.trap: Counting bold versions as separate fonts. The question says not to.

steps: Use all four views; each shows faces hidden in the others.
Count flat faces first: top, bottom and each side face of each arm.
Then add each curved surface: grooves and tunnels count as one surface each.
The total is 21.
qs.trap: Missing faces visible in only one view.

steps: Apples a, oranges 3a: total 4a, so 4a is 44 or 48.
Apples split 1 : 2 (good : rotten), so a is a multiple of 3. Oranges split 2 : 1, so 3a is too.
a = 11 fails; a = 12 works: 4 good and 8 rotten apples, 24 good and 12 rotten oranges.
Total = 48.

qs.trap: Taking 44. Eleven apples cannot be split in the ratio 1 : 2.

steps: From the top: an octagon outline divided into triangles and quadrilaterals.
From the bottom: a square base surrounded by triangles.
Match each coloured face between views so you count it once.
The total is 13.
qs.trap: Counting the same face in two views twice. Use the colours to match.

steps: Price went from Rs 2 to Rs 32: 30 rises, so 30 years after 1989 is 2019.
In 2019 Moosa turned 60, so in 1989 he was 30.
He was then six times Lisa's age: Lisa was 5, born 1984.
Lisa turns 60 in 1984 + 60 = 2044.
qs.trap: Counting 32 − 2 + 1 years. Each year adds Rs 1, so 30 years.

steps: Join the three centres: an equilateral triangle of side 20.
The three 60° sectors inside it make half a circle: 0.5 × 3.1416 × 100 = 157.08.

steps: Each corner of the big square has a right triangle with hypotenuse 5 and one side 3.
The other side is 4 (a 3-4-5 triangle).
Big side = 3 + 4 = 7; area 49.
Outside the small square = 49 − 25 = 24. The key also accepts 49.

steps: Hour digits 1 + 2 = 3, shown 60 times: 180.
Tens of minutes: 0 to 5, each for 10 minutes: 15 × 10 = 150.
Units of minutes: 0 to 9, each 6 times: 45 × 6 = 270.

steps: PR = 10 is the circle's radius, so the rectangle's diagonal is 20.
The rhombus joins the midpoints of the rectangle's sides.
Each rhombus side is half the rectangle's diagonal: 10.
Perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40.

qs.trap: Trying to find the rectangle's sides. You only need its diagonal.

steps: List leaf types by shape: maple, oak, chestnut (fan of leaflets), monstera, simple oval and so on.
Tally each type, ignoring colour and size.
Find types with a tally of exactly 1.
Only 2 types appear once.
qs.trap: Counting a small leaf as a new type. Size does not matter here.

steps: Pick a distinctive feature and note which way it turns relative to another.
Rotate the figure in your mind and check each option.
A mirror image is not a rotation.
A and D are rotations.
qs.trap: Accepting a mirror image.

steps: A: "To do so in a way that will bring blessings and not destruction" implies doing it badly brings destruction. True.
B: "Man comes nearest to his God... when he utilizes his brain power". True.
C: "He has to follow closely nature's way to get the best". True.
D: "Any attempt [on our own terms] will bring violent destruction". True.
qs.trap: Rejecting statements that rephrase the quote. Implied means supported by it.

steps: Each edge tab must fit into a matching blank on the next piece.
The outside of the square must be flat on all sides.
Try each set, rotating pieces to fit.
Sets C (2, 2, 2, 2) and D (2, 2, 3, 4) work.
qs.trap: Forgetting that pieces can be rotated.

steps: Place the fixed people first: Parmar in plot 1, Nadkarni in the north-east plot.
Munshi and Bhandari are Nadkarni's neighbours; Patel is farthest from Nadkarni, with Sethuraman next to him.
Balram is on the west; the only plot left fixes Das.
A (Das in plot 5) must be true. B is also true: Munshi can be Parmar's neighbour.
qs.trap: Confusing "must" and "could". Check the wording of each option.

steps: Folding along a line puts one part on top of the other, giving half the outline.
Find the fold line for each option and unfold it in your mind.
Check that the unfolded shape is a letter of the same font.
B, C and D unfold into letters.
qs.trap: Forgetting the rotation step after folding.

steps: R needs 8 minutes: P does 8 rounds, Q does 6. All end at the gate together: D true.
P gains half a round a minute on R: laps it at 2, 4 and 6 minutes, so 3 times. A true.
P gains a quarter round a minute on Q: laps it at 4 minutes only. B true.
Q laps R at 4 minutes, when R is at the gate, not the tree. C false.

rounds</text><line x1="2" y1="80" x2="232" y2="80" stroke="#E8DFC8" stroke-width="0.6" stroke-linecap="round" /></svg>
qs.trap: Counting the meeting at the end. The question excludes start and end.

steps: A: the figures clearly show keeping apart. True.
B: figures are drawn without gender cues and wear masks. True.
C: the figures do not show a range of ages, so "age inclusive" is not shown.
D: one poster cannot show all safety measures (hand washing, for example).
qs.trap: Choosing D for a good poster. "All measures" is too strong.

steps: Spinning fast, each colour blends into a ring at its distance from the centre.
Both sides show as the spinner turns over.
Work out the rings from each side's pattern.
B and C show the right rings.
qs.trap: Expecting to see the original shapes while it spins.

steps: Pick the corner where the three visible faces meet.
Check each net: do those faces meet at one corner with the patterns turned the same way?
Check opposite faces too.
B and C fold correctly.
qs.trap: Checking faces but not their orientation.

steps: Copper conducts heat far better than steel, so a copper base heats food faster and more evenly.
That saves energy: C is true.
A and B put steel at the bottom, the wrong way round.
D is false: induction needs a magnetic base such as steel; copper alone does not work on induction.
qs.trap: Choosing D. Copper is not magnetic, so it does not heat on induction by itself.

steps: Try cutting each shape into 4 smaller copies at half size.
Each copy must be the same shape, without flipping.
If the copies fill the shape exactly, it is a rep-tile.
B, C and D work.
qs.trap: Allowing flipped copies, which the question rules out.

steps: Two views do not fix a solid completely; several objects can share them.
Check each option's outline from the top and from the front.
Hidden differences (seen only from the side) do not matter.
All four options match.
qs.trap: Expecting only one answer. Two views can match many solids.

steps: Duration = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 seconds, so A (3 seconds) is false.
B: each dot is white for 4 frames per loop (from the animation). True.
C: at 8 fps the loop takes 3 s, so it plays slower, not faster. False.
D: 6 frames at 3 fps also lasts 2 s. True.
qs.trap: Thinking fewer frames per second is faster. It is slower.

steps: Identify each squiggle by a distinctive curl.
Rotate each sheet in your mind to match the options.
If a squiggle cannot be matched by rotation, it is different.
A and C contain different squiggles.
qs.trap: Forgetting that the sheets may be rotated.

steps: Trace the route on the map with your pencil, counting turnings carefully.
"Second right" means skip the first right turn and take the next.
Note the signals she passes in order.
She visits R4 before R2 and ends at R3: C and D.
qs.trap: Counting the junction you are on as the first turning.

steps: B: all mothers are female; some doctors are female and some are mothers.
C: all parrots are birds; some pets are birds and some are parrots.
A: dosa is a food and snacks are food: all nested, no partial overlap.
D: designers, teachers and painters only overlap; none sits fully inside another.
qs.trap: Checking only one pair of sets. All three relationships must match.

steps: The pyramid's apex is the centre of the cube, because its height is half the side.
Opposite face: lose 1 face, gain 4 triangles: 9 − 1 + 4 = 12.
Adjacent face: both pyramids share one triangle on the common edge, which disappears.
So 9 − 1 + 4 − 2 = 10. Possible counts: 10 or 12.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 104" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="6" width="228" height="32" rx="4" fill="#DDF0E6" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="19" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Opposite faces</text><text x="10" y="32" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">9 − 1 + 4 = 12</text><rect x="4" y="44" width="228" height="32" rx="4" fill="#FFE3CF" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="57" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Adjacent faces</text><text x="10" y="70" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">shared inner triangle cancels: 10</text><text x="118" y="98" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="middle">Each pyramid's apex is the cube's centre.</text></svg>
qs.trap: Forgetting the adjacent case, where a shared inner face disappears.

steps: Near a corner, four faces meet, so the cut is a square.
Through the middle, parallel to a face, the cut is a hexagon.
A tilted cut gives a pentagon.
A triangle needs a corner where three faces meet; octahedron corners have four.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 126" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="4" width="228" height="26" rx="3" fill="#DDF0E6" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="15" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Near a corner</text><text x="10" y="26" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">square (4 faces meet there)</text><rect x="4" y="34" width="228" height="26" rx="3" fill="#DDF0E6" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="45" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Parallel to a face, through the middle</text><text x="10" y="56" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">hexagon</text><rect x="4" y="64" width="228" height="26" rx="3" fill="#DDF0E6" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="75" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Tilted cut</text><text x="10" y="86" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">pentagon</text><rect x="4" y="94" width="228" height="26" rx="3" fill="#F8DEDA" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="105" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Any cut</text><text x="10" y="116" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">never a triangle: no corner has 3 faces</text></svg>
qs.trap: Thinking a triangular face means a triangular cut is possible.

steps: Look at the gaps in each row.
Each piece can fill gaps only in its own shape.
Try each set and count the complete rows.
Set C completes the most rows.
qs.trap: Rotating pieces, which is not allowed.

steps: Logo questions test small details: spacing, angles, overlaps.
Compare the options feature by feature.
Recall the real logo from everyday life.
D is correct.
qs.trap: Choosing by general look.

steps: P: covers most of the subcontinent in ancient times: Mauryan.
Q: southern India and across the sea to Sri Lanka and South-East Asia: Chola.
R: south of the Tungabhadra in the Deccan: Vijayanagar.
S: north and centre in the 1600s: Mughal.
qs.trap: Mixing up the Chola and Pallava empires. The Chola reach across the sea is the clue.

steps: Objects nearer the light cast bigger, blurrier shadows; nearer the screen, smaller and sharper.
Note each object's new distance in arrangement 2.
Overlaps follow the new order from the light.
B shows this.
qs.trap: Keeping shadow sizes the same when distances change.

steps: The handle must match the mug's perspective: the same ellipse angle.
Its ends must meet the mug at the right heights.
Check the thickness and curve.
B fits.
qs.trap: Choosing a handle drawn from a different viewpoint.

steps: Look at how each letter is built or changed from the last.
Find the rule: strokes added, removed, or rotated.
Apply it to the last letter.
The answer is P.
qs.trap: Looking at alphabet order only. The shapes carry the rule.

steps: The front wheel steers, so its track wiggles more.
The rear wheel follows, cutting the corners: its track is smoother, inside the front one.
One line belongs to neither tyre.
Blue is front, green is rear.
qs.trap: Choosing the smoother line as the front. The rear smooths the front's wiggles.

steps: Seen from a low angle, things far away look squashed.
To look right, the artist stretches parts that are seen at a slant.
Unfolded, the ladder looks distorted.
Option C shows the right distortion.
qs.trap: Expecting an ordinary ladder drawing.

steps: Outer lanes are longer around a bend.
So outer runners start further ahead (a staggered start).
Each step forward must make up the extra distance of that lane.
Option C has the right stagger.
qs.trap: Lining everyone up straight.

steps: Each face of P has 9 squares: 5 green, 4 white (56% green).
Each face of Q has 25 squares: 13 green, 12 white (52% green).
The cubes are the same size, so compare fractions.
P has more green surface than Q.

qs.trap: Thinking more cubes means more green. Compare fractions of the same area.

steps: At 45°, a shadow's length equals the height of the part casting it.
Read heights from the shadow lengths in each direction.
Match the heights to an option.
D matches.
qs.trap: Ignoring the shadow lengths.

steps: Track one element at a time.
Find how it changes each step.
Apply the change once more.
B fits.
qs.trap: Tracking everything at once.

steps: A weak pose is mirrored: left and right sides do the same thing.
A weak silhouette has limbs inside the body outline, so the action is unclear.
Check each pose for both faults.
B has both faults.
qs.trap: Choosing a pose for its expression. Only the two named aspects count.

steps: The minute hand moves 6° a minute; the hour hand 0.5°.
The minute hand gains 5.5° a minute.
To be opposite again, it must gain a full 360°.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 126" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="4" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="18" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Minute hand: 6° per minute</text><rect x="4" y="28" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="42" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Hour hand: 0.5° per minute</text><rect x="4" y="52" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="66" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Minute hand gains 5.5° per minute</text><rect x="4" y="76" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="90" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">To be opposite again it must gain 360°</text><rect x="4" y="100" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#FFE3CF" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="114" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.4" font-weight="700" fill="#FF6B0A" text-anchor="start">360 ÷ 5.5 = 65.45 min = 65 min 27 s</text></svg>
qs.trap: Answering 60 minutes. The hour hand moves too.

steps: Water can only rise to the lowest opening: usually the spout tip.
A tall body does not help if the spout starts low.
Compare spout heights.
A has the highest spout opening.
qs.trap: Choosing the biggest kettle. The spout height limits the water.

steps: Look for the rule across the row and down the column.
Test it on all rows.
Apply it to the gap.
D fits.
qs.trap: Using one row only.

steps: When landing, the nose is slightly raised.
The rear wheels touch the runway first.
Flaps are down and the plane is close to the ground.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a nose-down plane. That would land on its front wheel first.

steps: Each step adds one side, keeping the same pieces plus one new cut.
Pieces move without rotating.
Look at how the pieces shift each time.
C continues the pattern.
qs.trap: Rotating pieces, which the question rules out.

steps: Do one rotation at a time and sketch the result.
Clockwise means as seen from the positive end of the axis, looking at the origin.
Track one distinctive feature through all three turns.
A is the result.
qs.trap: Doing the rotations all at once in your head.

steps: On straight parts along x, x changes fastest.
Where the road turns along y, x changes slowly or not at all.
The graph must never jump.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a straight line. A winding road changes the x speed.

steps: Compare each small triangle's area with the large one using their side lengths.
Area scales with the square of the side.
Add five small areas and subtract from the large one.
About 44% is empty.
qs.trap: Scaling area with side length instead of its square.

steps: Check opposite faces in the net: they never touch.
In each cube, check that the three visible faces could meet at one corner.
Check pattern directions.
B cannot come from the net.
qs.trap: Forgetting the question asks for NOT.

steps: When a ball hits the ground, it squashes; as it leaves, it stretches.
The volume stays the same; only the shape changes.
This is one of the 12 principles of animation.
Squash and Stretch.
qs.trap: Choosing "Stretching". The principle includes both squash and stretch.

steps: Two loops joined at right angles and cut down the middle make a square frame.
Picture each loop splitting into two bands joined at the corners.
This is a classic paper trick.
D shows a square.
qs.trap: Expecting two separate loops.

steps: Mirroring upward makes an upside-down pyramid above the first.
Turning 135° is the same as 45° for a square base: the bases form an 8-pointed star from above.
Lowering them makes their sloping faces cross.
A shows the result.
qs.trap: Treating 135° as unique. Square symmetry repeats every 90°.

steps: A cylinder mirror stretches and curves what it reflects.
The part of the word nearest the cylinder looks largest in the reflection.
The reflection is also mirrored left to right.
A shows this.
qs.trap: Expecting a flat-mirror image.

steps: Find where the mirror is: below or beside.
Reflect each part across that line.
Check two distinctive details.
D is correct.
qs.trap: Reflecting in the wrong direction.

steps: A square with a corner at the centre of another equal square always covers exactly a quarter of it, however it is turned.
Use this to find the overlapping parts.
Count the quarters that remain shaded.
The shaded part is 1/4.
qs.trap: Trying to calculate the tilted shapes. The quarter rule makes it simple.

steps: Find the rule linking the given items.
Check it on every example.
Apply it to the missing item.
D fits.
qs.trap: Building a rule from one example only.

steps: Start order, front to back: P, Q, S, R.
P is out. R overtakes Q (and S): R, Q, S.
S overtakes Q just before the end: R, S, Q.
Q is last, so Q is slowest and wins.

steps: Compare small details: shapes, spacing, letter forms.
Recall the real logo carefully.
Eliminate options with one wrong detail.
B is correct.
qs.trap: Choosing by overall look.
